question: Your team moved nightly test generation in the CI/CD pipeline to the Message Batches API. A scheduled job submits the batch at 1 a.m., and the generated tests usually return within an hour, well before the 9 a.m. team review. Last night the batch finished at 3 p.m., and the team missed the review. A developer opens a bug ticket against the batch job. What best explains the late results?

options.text: The batch broke the guaranteed latency SLA of the Message Batches API, so the delay points to a fault that the team should report.
options.reason: The guide states that the Message Batches API has no guaranteed latency SLA, so there is no SLA that this batch could break.

options.text: The batch job omitted custom_id fields on its requests, so the Message Batches API placed the whole batch at a lower processing priority.
options.reason: The guide describes custom_id as a field for correlating batch request and response pairs, not as a setting that controls processing priority.

options.text: The Message Batches API has no guaranteed latency SLA, so a batch that finishes within the 24-hour processing window is behaving as designed.
options.reason: The guide states that the Message Batches API has an up to 24-hour processing window with no guaranteed latency SLA, so a finish at 3 p.m. is expected behavior and not a bug.

options.text: The test generation requests called tools mid-request, and the Message Batches API paused each request until the tool results were returned.
options.reason: The guide states that the batch API does not support multi-turn tool calling within a request, so it cannot pause to execute tools and return their results.
